paragraphs.en: with ruthenium trichloride in an aqueous caustic solution containing starting material and purging chlorine gas.
paragraphs.notes: Tail of a paragraph that began on p10. The page opens mid-sentence on the word 'with', so this entry carries no marker and I did not guess the number it would have had. The fragment names ruthenium trichloride as the ruthenium source, while the paragraph below it and both drawings on this page use RuO2. This page alone does not state how the two relate; the sentence that would say so is on p10, so a later pass must join this fragment to its head before reading anything into the difference.

paragraphs.zh: In at least one embodiment, 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST) of formula (IV) can be oxidized to 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III) with RuO2 as a catalyst and cheap and readily available sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) as an oxidant.In certain embodiments, the mixture of 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST) of formula (IV),RuO2 catalyst and sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) can be heated to reflux temperature under stirring for about more than 2 hours, 3 hours, 4 hours, or 5 hours, preferably in the range of about 2 hours to about 8 hours, more preferably for about 6 hours to about 8 hours.
paragraphs.en: In at least one embodiment, 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST) of formula (IV) can be oxidized to 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III) with RuO2 as a catalyst and cheap and readily available sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) as an oxidant.In certain embodiments, the mixture of 2-nitro-4-methylsulfonyl toluene (NMST) of formula (IV),RuO2 catalyst and sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) can be heated to reflux temperature under stirring for about more than 2 hours, 3 hours, 4 hours, or 5 hours, preferably in the range of about 2 hours to about 8 hours, more preferably for about 6 hours to about 8 hours.
paragraphs.notes: Marker transcribed as printed, not zero-padded. Printing oddities kept verbatim: 'oxidant.In' has no space after the full stop, and 'formula (IV),RuO2' has no space after the comma. The paragraph spells the same moiety two ways one line apart, exactly as brief section 8 warns: 'methylsulfonyl' with an f for the toluene and 'methylsulphonyl' with a ph for the benzoic acid, and it repeats the f spelling for the toluene later in the same paragraph. Neither was normalised. RuO2 and NaOCl are printed with a subscript 2 on RuO2; transcribed as a plain digit. Left margin carries line numbers 5 and 10 against this paragraph; they are furniture and were kept out of the text.

paragraphs.zh: In certain embodiments, there is provided a process for preparation of an enol ester of formula (II) by reaction of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III) with 1, 3-cyclohexanedione. This method is extremely advantageous over the prior art methods for the preparation of enol ester, in that it does not require the additional step of converting NMSBA to an intermediate of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoyl chloride (NMSBC).
paragraphs.en: In certain embodiments, there is provided a process for preparation of an enol ester of formula (II) by reaction of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoic acid (NMSBA) of formula (III) with 1, 3-cyclohexanedione. This method is extremely advantageous over the prior art methods for the preparation of enol ester, in that it does not require the additional step of converting NMSBA to an intermediate of 2-nitro-4-methylsulphonyl benzoyl chloride (NMSBC).
paragraphs.notes: Marker transcribed as printed, not zero-padded. 'with 1, 3-cyclohexanedione' is printed with a space after the comma and is kept as printed. This paragraph uses the ph spelling 'methylsulphonyl' for both the benzoic acid and the benzoyl chloride, with no f spelling in it at all, so the two spellings are not distributed evenly down the page. Left margin carries line number 15 against this paragraph. The paragraph ends complete, with '(NMSBC).', so the page does not end mid-sentence; the last inked content on the page is the second scheme and its formula labels.

drawings.notes: One arrow, one reagent line, printed as the single string 'NaOCl / RuO2' above the arrow with the slash as printed and a subscript 2 on RuO2. Nothing at all is printed below the arrow; I checked the band under the arrow line down to the formula labels and it is blank ink, so reagents_below is empty because the position is empty, not because I could not read it. The arrow line is degraded to broken dotted ink over its whole length but terminates in one solid filled arrowhead, so it is recorded as solid per brief section 9 and not as dashed. Labels printed under the drawings, without parentheses: 'Formula IV' under the left structure, which is the NMST starting material, and 'Formula III' under the right structure, which is the NMSBA product. Neither label prints the abbreviation itself; NMST and NMSBA appear only in the prose. All ring positions were read off the drawing at 4x magnification, not inferred: in both structures the hexagon is drawn pointy-top, the ring-junction substituent sits on the top vertex, NO2 sits on the vertex one bond clockwise from it, and SO2CH3 sits on the bottom vertex, which is three bonds round, hence C4. Cross-check against the prose on this page was run and found no disagreement: the prose names sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) as oxidant and RuO2 as catalyst and the arrow writes both. Worth flagging against the brief, which reports that p15 labels the same transformation only 'Oxidant / RuO2' and so has a real discrepancy: on this page the arrow names NaOCl explicitly, so this page has no such discrepancy. The arrow does not distinguish which of the two is the catalyst and which the oxidant; only the prose does.

drawings.notes: Second and last drawing on the page, and the last inked content on the page. between_markers closes on null because no numbered paragraph follows it on this sheet; the next one is on p12. The arrow is completely bare: nothing is printed above it and nothing below it. I magnified the band above and the band below the arrow line separately and both are blank, so both reagent lists are empty because the positions are empty, not because they were unreadable. Like the first arrow the line is degraded to dots but ends in one solid filled arrowhead, so it is recorded as solid, not dashed. A printed plus sign sits between the 1st and 2nd structures. Labels printed under the drawings, without parentheses: 'Formula III' under the leftmost structure and 'Formula II' under the product. The middle reactant, cyclohexane-1,3-dione, carries no printed label at all. The 1st structure here is drawn identically to the 2nd structure of the first drawing on this page, same substituent positions, and both are labelled Formula III. The middle ring is drawn as the saturated 1,3-diketone with two exocyclic C double bond O and no ring double bond and no enol OH, so no enol tautomer was read into it; the enol geometry appears only in the product, where the ring double bond is drawn explicitly on the side bearing the ester oxygen. Cross-check against the prose was run: paragraph [0036] describes exactly this reaction, NMSBA of formula (III) with 1, 3-cyclohexanedione giving the enol ester of formula (II), and the drawing agrees with it on every count, so no disagreement to report. The prose names no solvent, catalyst or condition for this step and the arrow carries none either, so nothing is drawn that is not written and nothing written that is not drawn.
